history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed (Buddhist monastery). Ralong is Sikkim's first Kagyu-sect monastery: the fourth Chogyal Gyurmed Namgyal founded the old Karma Rabtenling gompa around 1730 after meeting the 12th Karmapa in Tibet (the Sikkim Ecclesiastical Affairs Dept. gives 1730; travel sources and Wikipedia list the old gompa's establishment as 1768 — founding date conflict, verify). The original gompa sits ~1.5 km from the town; the present large Ralong Palchen Choling monastic institute was built by the 12th Gyaltsab Rinpoche and completed in 1995, and holds an extensive collection of paintings and thangkas.

name: Ralong Monastery
town_description: Ralong (also spelled Ralang) is a small mountain village about 6 km from Ravangla in South Sikkim, surrounded by forests and hot springs along the Rangit valley, and home to one of Sikkim's oldest Kagyu Buddhist monasteries.

travel.road: ~6 km from Ravangla; reachable by taxi/shared jeep via Ravangla, or onward from Siliguri/Gangtok by SNT bus

visitor_information.best_time: October to May; festival season September–December
visitor_information.opening_hours: Travel sites list daily 08:00–17:00 for the new monastery — verify locally
